implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.__init__ defaults to rows=6, cols=7 and creates a 6x7 grid.
Game.players holds two Player objects and Game.switch_player toggles current_index between 0 and 1.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players choose columns by typing a number
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.get_player_move prompts with "choose a column 1‑{}" and parses the input as an integer.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Validate column choices (range and not full)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.get_player_move uses Board.is_valid_column and prints specific error messages for out‑of‑range or full columns.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Drop discs with gravity (to the lowest empty cell)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.drop_disc iterates from bottom row upward, placing the disc in the first EMPTY slot.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Update and display the board after each move
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.play calls Board.render after each successful drop.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line of four discs
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.check_win checks four directions (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (1,-1) and counts consecutive matching discs.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect a draw when the grid is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full returns True when the top row has no EMPTY cells; Game.play ends with a draw message.

implemented_requirements.requirement: End the game on win, draw, or player quit
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.play returns after a win, after a draw, or when get_player_move returns None (quit/EOF).
main.py creates a Game instance and calls game.play() when executed as __main__.

judge.summary: The repository provides a complete, runnable Connect Four implementation. All core gameplay mechanics—grid size, turn alternation, numeric column input, move validation, gravity, win/draw detection, and graceful termination—are present and backed by concrete code. The code appears syntactically correct and ready to execute, so the submission meets the benchmark requirements.
